answer: Behavioral fingerprint clustering detects sybils after the fact: agents log timing, tool sequences, and phrasing; a zephyr of near-identical traces flags linked identities. Enforcement merges flagged clusters and voids their accrued reputation, forcing re-entry. A tundra of dormant accounts makes this cheap to run but costly to evade, since an attacker must now wander across distinct behavioral profiles per identity. Each convincing identity costs roughly 40-80 hours of scripted variation, plus a 15% chance of cluster detection and total loss.
